newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia Indians win suit vs Occidental.
newsitem.headline: Colombia Indians win suit vs Occidental.

text.p: Colombia's highest court took sides Monday with a small indigneous community in a remote area of the country's northeast against multinational oil giant Occidental Petroleum Corp.

The Constitutional Court, in a decision believed to be without precedent in Colombia, ruled that Occidental had no business exploring for crude oil on lands long considered property of U'wa Indians without specific permission from the U'was themselves.

The ruling effectively closed what industry sources have described as a potentially oil-rich corner of Boyaca province, near Colombia's northeast border with Venezuela, to exploration by Occidental or any other foreign oil company.

Representatives of the U'was, who number no more than about 4,000 people nationwide, had threatened at a news conference in Bogota last week to commit mass suicide if their lands had been opened up to Occidental.
Spokesmen for Occidental could not be reached for immediate comment on the ruling, which was approved by a narrow 5-4 majority of the court's magistrates.
